newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka massacre survivor identifies soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka massacre survivor identifies soldiers.

text.p: An 18-year-old Sri Lankan girl who survived a massacre of Tamil civilians in eastern Trincomalee a year ago has identified two soldiers involved in the killings, court officials said on Thursday.
Arunasalam Paramarani told a court in Trincomalee that the soldiers shot her mother dead and wounded her cousin.
Magistrate S.A. Liyanage last month charged eight soldiers with the murder of 25 Tamil civilians, including women and children, in the village of Kumarapuram, on February 11, 1996.
The soldiers were also charged with the attempted murder of 26 civilians wounded in the attack.

Military officials said the troops apparently shot dead the civilians in retaliation for the killing of two soldiers by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels near Kumarapuram, 30 km (20 miles) south of Trincomalee, the same day.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
The government, which has cracked down on human rights abuses by its security forces, ordered an inquiry into the massacre after complaints from Tamil parliamentarians.
Three other witnesses, out of 120 to be called in total, gave evidence at the inquiry on Wednesday. The hearing was postponed until April 30.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is higher.
